question: Should cities encourage people and businesses to keep more honeybee hives to help pollinators?
answer: Hives make people care. A beekeeper learns which flowers bloom when, pushes for planting, and notices poisoning and disease before anyone else. Honeybees still pollinate many crops, and city gardens and parks give them a varied diet with fewer pesticides than farmland. A hive on an office roof keeps pollinators in public view.
move: Whichever side you took, it turns on how many flowers each hive must share.
ask: Which good-feeling thing I do have I never checked actually helps what it claims to?
counterpoint: Honeybees are one farmed species; the pollinators in trouble are wild bees, and hives compete with them for the same pollen and nectar and can pass diseases to bumblebees. Geldmann and González-Varo argued in Science that keeping honeybees is agriculture, not conservation. Where hives outgrow the flowers, wild bees lose.
reference: Geldmann & González-Varo, Conserving honey bees does not help wildlife, Science, 2018
